title: Tag and keyword case matching engine

history.detail:
CONDITIONAL: CONDITIONAL PASS â€” audit round 1, commit 0583f53 (branch sprint-4-case-matcher).

Scope audited: lib/concern-fact-pattern-bridge.ts, lib/case-matcher.ts, the
MatchedTag/MatchResult and HumanRightsCodeGround changes in lib/types.ts, and
both new test files. Sprint file re-read fresh immediately before this verdict.

All 15 requirements met. All 12 acceptance criteria confirmed. Vitest: 27/27
pass, run twice, identical. tsc --noEmit clean. data/seed-library.json and
package.json untouched. No embeddings/vector/model dependency. Matcher is pure
(no network, fs, clock, randomness), never reads groundTags, never branches on
isPlaceholder. Bridge is a single exported commented constant and is genuinely
many-to-many in both directions (medical-absence -> 3 tags;
disability-accommodation reached from all 4 concerns). types.ts changes are
bounded to requirements 12 and 13.

REQUIRED BEFORE SHIP â€” two fixes, both small:

1. [MEDIUM] The relevance threshold is never exercised at its boundary.
   lib/case-matcher.test.ts:72 "returns empty when nothing clears the relevance
   threshold" uses a situation with an empty narrative, all three facts
   not-reported, and a case whose only fact-pattern tag is outside the bridged
   set. That scores exactly 0. Every other test scores >= 10 (one fact-pattern
   hit = factPatternWeight = 10 = relevanceThreshold). No test produces a score
   strictly between 0 and threshold, so the suite proves only "zero overlap
   returns empty", which is true of any filter, and does not pin the threshold
   at all: any relevanceThreshold from 1 to 10 passes the entire suite
   unchanged. Requirement 8 is the one requirement that exists to stop a weak
   case reaching a user, and it is the one with no test behind it. Add a case
   with keyword overlap only and no bridged fact-pattern overlap â€” 1 to 4
   shared keywords scores 2 to 8, below threshold â€” asserting an empty result.

2. [MEDIUM] Tie-breaking uses String.prototype.localeCompare with no locale
   argument (lib/case-matcher.ts:126). localeCompare resolves against the host's
   default locale and ICU build, so ordering is a property of the machine, not
   of the code. Requirement 6 asks for the same Situation and library to always
   produce the same ordered result. Harmless against the current lowercase-ASCII
   placeholder ids, and it does satisfy the "explicit, not incidental to
   iteration order" half of the requirement, but it is not deterministic by
   construction, and Sprint 7 replaces every id in the library. On a tool whose
   output is which two cases a person is shown, ordering should not depend on
   the build environment. Use a plain codepoint comparison (a < b ? -1 : a > b
   ? 1 : 0) or pass an explicit locale.

MINOR â€” fix while in there, not a gate:

3. [LOW] lib/case-matcher.test.ts:75-76 comment states "age-termination is not
   among medical-absence's bridged patterns". It is â€” medical-absence bridges to
   disability-accommodation, family-status, and age-termination. The test itself
   is correct (the fixture is tagged harassment-poisoned-work-environment); only
   the comment is wrong. It sits in the test documenting threshold behaviour, so
   it is the comment most likely to mislead whoever tunes the bridge later.

FOR MASTER CONTROLLER / CHANG â€” not a defect, do not fix in this sprint:

relevanceThreshold (10) equals factPatternWeight (10), so a single bridged
fact-pattern hit clears the gate on its own. Combined with a deliberately broad
bridge, disability-accommodation is reachable from all four concerns, this means
essentially any situation clears the threshold against essentially any case
carrying that tag. The threshold does almost no filtering work in practice.
Requirement 8's mechanism is correctly implemented and weight tuning is
explicitly out of scope (no benchmark set exists), so this is not a failure of
this sprint. It is, however, the specific interaction that decides whether
requirement 8's intent, an empty result beats a bad case, actually holds once
Sprint 7 lands real citations. This belongs with the bridge review already
flagged in the sprint's Dependencies section, and should be settled before
Sprint 6 renders anything.

Placeholder library data was treated as the expected input throughout, per the
sprint's standing instruction. No finding recorded about case content. Noted
only as context: the four placeholder records carry the literal title
[VERIFIED CASE CITATION NEEDED] and near-empty keyFinding text, so the keyword
path contributes nothing against the current library and all matching today is
fact-pattern-only. That is the sprint's stated position (logic provable, quality
not), not a defect, but it does mean the keyword scoring path has no exercise
outside synthetic fixtures until Sprint 7.

Re-audit required after fixes 1 and 2. Do not run /sprint-dev-done on this
verdict.

PASS: PASS â€” audit round 2, commit 9d00b62 (branch sprint-4-case-matcher), clean tree.

Sprint file unchanged since round 1: blob cf11f8e44a4f7fdf16a973e91d2b92badd83f17f
is identical at 0583f53, at 9d00b62, and in the worktree. Requirements did not
move, so this re-audit is scoped to the diff between rounds, as the agent brief
allows for an isolated amendment.

Round-1 findings, all three closed:

1. [WAS MEDIUM] Relevance threshold boundary now tested. New case at
   lib/case-matcher.test.ts:89, "returns empty for a score strictly between zero
   and the threshold". Verified non-vacuous rather than taken on trust: the
   fixture case carries factPatternTags: [] so the fact-pattern loop contributes
   nothing, and the four narrative tokens all clear the length-3 filter and the
   stopword set, matching four case tokens for 4 x keywordWeight 2 = 8, one
   scoring step below relevanceThreshold 10. Score is 8, not 0, so the test would
   actually catch a lowered threshold â€” which is precisely what the round-1
   version could not do. Reachable scores are all even (weights 10 and 2), so
   thresholds 9 and 10 remain behaviourally identical; that is a property of the
   weights, not a gap in the test.

2. [WAS MEDIUM] localeCompare replaced with an explicit codepoint comparison at
   lib/case-matcher.ts:124-128. Ordering no longer depends on the host's default
   locale or ICU build. Requirement 6 is now satisfied by construction rather
   than by the accident of today's ids being lowercase ASCII, which matters
   because Sprint 7 replaces every id in the library.

3. [WAS LOW] Comment at lib/case-matcher.test.ts:75-77 corrected. It now names
   harassment-poisoned-work-environment, which genuinely is outside
   medical-absence's bridged patterns, and states the resulting score is zero.

Nothing crept in alongside the fixes. The diff between rounds is exactly the
comparator, the new test, the corrected comment, and the script-owned state
file. lib/types.ts, lib/concern-fact-pattern-bridge.ts, data/seed-library.json
and package.json are all untouched since round 1.

Full re-verification against all 15 requirements and all 12 acceptance criteria:
all met. Vitest 28/28 pass, run twice, identical. tsc --noEmit clean. Matcher
remains pure â€” no network, filesystem, clock, or randomness. Never reads
groundTags; never branches on isPlaceholder (the only occurrences of either
identifier are in doc comments stating they are not used). No embeddings, vector
store, or model call in the diff or in package.json, and no new dependency.
Bridge is a single exported commented constant, many-to-many in both directions.
MatchedTag is the discriminated shape from requirement 12. lib/types.ts changes
remain bounded to requirements 12 and 13.

CARRIED FORWARD FOR MASTER CONTROLLER / CHANG â€” unchanged from round 1, still
not a defect and deliberately not fixed here:

relevanceThreshold (10) equals factPatternWeight (10), so one bridged
fact-pattern hit clears the gate alone, and disability-accommodation is reachable
from all four concerns. The threshold does little filtering in practice. Weight
tuning is explicitly out of scope with no benchmark set to tune against, so this
does not block the sprint. It decides whether requirement 8's intent holds once
Sprint 7 lands real citations, and belongs with the bridge review already flagged
in the sprint's Dependencies.

New, same category, noted while verifying the boundary fixture: the seed-library
schema puts no minItems on factPatternTags (lib/seed-library-schema.ts:76-79), so
a record with zero fact-pattern tags is schema-valid. Such a record can never be
reached through the bridge and would need five or more keyword hits to surface at
all. That is Sprint 2's schema, outside this diff, and requirement 14 says flag
rather than fix in passing â€” so, flagged. It also means the round-2 boundary
fixture represents a state the real library could actually hold, which is why I
consider the test realistic rather than synthetic.

Standing limitation, restated because it does not go away with a PASS: I
confirmed the bridge is many-to-many, exported, and commented. I did not confirm
that performance-management plausibly implicates age/termination. That is law,
not code, and no gate in this workflow can check it. Chang should review the
bridge constant before Sprint 6 renders anything derived from it.

Cleared for /sprint-dev-done, then Pipeman.

PASS: GroundTruth live test, sprint 4, round 1. Verdict PASS.

All four GroundTruth acceptance criteria pass. No regression to Sprints 1 or 3,
and the matcher has not leaked into anything a user can reach.

ENVIRONMENT
Tested 2026-08-17, Chrome (Claude in Chrome extension).
URL: https://bc-employer-issue-guide.vercel.app/ (intake at /intake).
Vercel production deployment: "Sprint 4: record ship (commit 1ba3bbf)",
status "Ready", 14s, Production, built from 9411a20 on main.

COMMIT LINEAGE -- VERIFIED, NOT ASSUMED
Recorded against 1ba3bbf. Vercel built 9411a20 ("Sprint 4: record ship (commit
1ba3bbf)"). App code byte-identical:
  git diff --stat 1ba3bbf 9411a20 -- . ':(exclude)docs/**'   -> empty

NO-UI CLAIM ESTABLISHED AT THE SOURCE, NOT ACCEPTED FROM THE HANDOFF
  git diff --stat 13bf6d0 1ba3bbf -- app/ components/   -> EMPTY
Zero bytes changed in the UI between Sprint 3's deployed commit and Sprint 4's.
grep over app/ and components/ for case-matcher / concern-fact-pattern /
matchCases / MatchResult returns no matches -- nothing wires the matcher to a
screen. data/seed-library.json untouched by this diff.
lib/types.ts did move (25 lines), so I checked the bound rather than assuming it:
the diff is the requirement-12 MatchedTag discriminated union plus the
requirement-13 doc-comment correction. No type consumed by the intake UI
(Situation, IntakeMetadata, ConcernCategory) changed shape.

CHECKS (verbatim results + evidence)

[x] AC: deployed app still builds and loads at the recorded URL with no console
    errors -- PASS. Deployment "Ready" in 14s; "/", "/about" and "/intake" all
    return HTTP 200. Console findings are the app's own: none. See the console
    section below, which is the one place I want the record to be precise.

[x] AC: the full Sprint 3 intake flow still completes end to end, including
    per-prompt validation, the "nothing yet" affordance, and back-navigation
    preserving data -- PASS, all parts re-tested live rather than inferred from
    the empty UI diff.
    - Step 1 empty -> Next: blocked, message verbatim "Missing: employment
      status, length of employment, whether formal complaints have been
      lodged." role=alert present, 1 aria-invalid, aria-describedby resolving.
    - Step 2 with nothing selected -> Next: blocked, verbatim "Select at least
      one concern to continue."
    - Per-prompt validation: 184 characters in "what happened", prompts 2 and 3
      empty -> BLOCKED, "Intake complete" not reached, exactly TWO alerts
      (documentation, employer action), 2 aria-invalid. Prompt 1's own alert
      correctly absent since 184 >= its 100 minimum. This is the Sprint 3
      Amendment 2 behaviour and it is intact.
    - "Nothing yet / not applicable" on the documentation prompt: its textarea
      became disabled, its alert cleared immediately, flow proceeded.
    - Back-navigation: from step 3, Back -> step 2, Back -> step 1. Step 1 still
      held "Terminated", "7 years", "Yes" -- exactly what I entered. Forward
      again to step 3: the 184-character narrative was still intact. Retention
      holds in both directions.
    - Completion: Situation rendered with employment status "terminated",
      tenure "7 years", complaints "Yes", concerns "interpersonal-conflict,
      performance-management", narrative = prompts 1 and 3 joined, with the
      not-applicable documentation prompt correctly OMITTED rather than
      contributing an empty line.

[x] AC: Sprint 1 disclaimer banner still present throughout -- PASS.
    Present on step 1, step 2, step 3, the blocked/error states, and the
    completion screen. On the completion screen checked character-for-character:
    exact match, length 66, character at index 31 is code 8212 (U+2014 EM DASH),
    computed position sticky, rectTop 0.
    Server-rendered HTML (first paint) checked on "/", "/about" and "/intake",
    2 runs each: exactly ONE rendered banner tag per document, "sticky top-0
    z-50" present, HTTP 200 on all three.

[x] AC: NO CASE CONTENT OF ANY KIND IS USER-VISIBLE -- PASS. Treated as the
    falsifiable half of this gate and probed four ways, with one probe designed
    specifically for this sprint:

    1. Client bundles. Fetched and scanned all 9 shipped scripts, 719,072 bytes,
       for case content (BCHRT, "VERIFIED CASE CITATION NEEDED", each
       placeholder record id, seed-library, citationGuard, placeholderCount,
       Devine) AND for this sprint's matcher symbols (MATCH_CONFIG, matchCases,
       CONCERN_TO_FACT_PATTERN_BRIDGE, MatchedTag, case-matcher,
       concern-fact-pattern). ZERO hits on every one.
    2. THE VOCABULARY PROBE -- the sharp one for Sprint 4. The bridge maps
       intake concerns to LEGAL fact patterns, so if the bridge or matcher had
       leaked into the client, the legal vocabulary would appear alongside the
       intake vocabulary. Result: all four INTAKE values are present
       (medical-absence, schedule-flexibility, interpersonal-conflict,
       performance-management -- expected, they are the form's own options),
       and ZERO of the four LEGAL fact patterns appear anywhere
       (disability-accommodation, harassment-poisoned-work-environment,
       age-termination, family-status). The two vocabularies are still
       separated in the shipped artifact, exactly as Sprint 3's AC required and
       Sprint 4 preserves.
    3. Rendered output under a case that would produce matches. I deliberately
       completed the flow with concerns "interpersonal-conflict" and
       "performance-management" and a narrative mentioning conflict and age --
       inputs the bridge maps to harassment-poisoned-work-environment,
       disability-accommodation and age-termination. Nothing was surfaced. The
       completion screen shows no case, no citation, no score, no matchedTags,
       and no "related/similar/matched case" wording. Testing with inputs that
       WOULD match is what makes this criterion falsifiable rather than
       vacuous.
    4. Direct reachability. /data/seed-library.json, /seed-library.json,
       /lib/case-matcher.js, /api/match, /api/cases and /data/ all returned
       HTTP 404.

    No case surface, no matcher output. No scope violation.

PER THE SPRINT'S OWN INSTRUCTION
The acceptance criteria state up front that four isPlaceholder records with
0000 BCHRT 0 citations are the intended state and that neither gate should
record a finding about missing or unverified case content. I am not recording
one. I note only that no Dev-Team-authored case data appeared: the diff does not
touch data/seed-library.json at all, which is the standing Sprint 2 rule.

ISSUES FOUND
None blocking. Two observations, one of which I nearly mis-reported and want on
the record with its reasoning.

OBSERVATION 1 [LOW] -- there is a pre-hydration window where the intake form's
buttons are silently inert.
On my first attempt this round, clicking "Next" on an empty step 1 blocked the
advance but produced NO validation message -- not the message Sprint 3
produced. That looked like a validation regression and I nearly wrote it up as
one. It is not. I distinguished the two hypotheses before reporting: I filled
the step in and clicked Next, and it advanced correctly, proving React was
attached by then; then I reloaded, waited 3 seconds to settle, and clicked Next
once on an empty step 1 -- the message appeared verbatim, "Missing: employment
status, length of employment, whether formal complaints have been lodged.",
with role=alert and aria-invalid.
So the real behaviour is: clicks landing before hydration completes do nothing
at all, silently. That is inherent to server-rendered React and is not a Sprint 4
regression -- no Sprint 4 code touches the UI. But a real user who clicks Next
quickly on a slow connection gets no feedback whatsoever, and this is a form
whose whole job is telling people what is missing. Worth Master Controller's
attention as a small follow-up (disable the button until hydrated, or render
it from a client component that signals readiness), not a blocker, and not
attributable to this sprint.

OBSERVATION 2 [environmental, now proven, not the app] -- the console noise I
flagged in Sprint 3 is a browser extension, and this round I have the stack
trace to prove it rather than the circumstantial argument I offered last time.
During interactive testing, six instances appeared of:
  "Error: A listener indicated an asynchronous response by returning true, but
   the message channel closed before a response was received"
reported against /intake:0:0 with no application stack, clustered at the exact
timestamps of my tool calls. Then on a clean reload with a 6-second settle and
no page script executed by me, the console showed:
  "RegisterClientLocalizationsError
   at rejected (chrome-extension://nbmoafcmbajniiapeidgficgifbfmjfo/client/
   main.js:63:10)"
That is an explicit chrome-extension:// origin. An extension is injecting into
this page and throwing; the message-channel errors are the same layer, which is
why they carry no application stack. The app itself performs no async messaging.
The app's own console error count is ZERO. Recording the extension id so nobody
has to re-derive this a third time -- and noting that it means "no console
errors" should always be assessed by origin here, not by raw count.

CONSISTENCY
Deterministic sprint, no AI and no network in the product path. Repetition run
where it could reveal something: server-HTML first-paint checks twice per route
across three routes, identical output; the full intake flow completed with a
different input set than Sprint 3's to avoid re-treading one path.

CARRIED FORWARD
Nothing new. The Sprint 3 focus-management observation (focus resets to BODY on
step advance) still stands and is unchanged by this sprint; I did not re-litigate
it here since no Sprint 4 code touches the UI.

VERDICT: PASS. Gate 2 clear.
Code ready. Not authorization to close -- /sprint-complete still requires the
user's explicit, real-time go-ahead via --user-said, and that is Dev Team's
command to run, not mine.

user_said=Yes, close Sprint 4. Both gates are green, no blocking findings, and the two non-blocking observations (pre-hydration silent-inert window, browser extension console noise) are confirmed non-issues for this sprint.
